chunks: And Jarir narrated from Ash'ath, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet, may God bless him and his family.
He said: The caliphs after me are twelve, like the number of chiefs of the Children of Israel.

key_terms.بَنِي إِسْرَائِيل: Children of Israel -- the twelve tribes of Israel each had an appointed chief (naqib)
key_terms.خُلَفَاء: Caliphs/successors -- in Shia understanding, this refers to the Twelve Imams, not political caliphs
key_terms.نُقَبَاء: Chiefs or leaders appointed by God from among the Children of Israel, as mentioned in Quran 5:12

ai.seo_question: What is the hadith of the Twelve Caliphs and how does it relate to the Twelve Imams in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This is a famous prophetic hadith (hadith al-khulafa al-ithna ashar) in which the Prophet Muhammad explicitly states that there will be twelve caliphs/successors after him, comparing their number to the twelve chiefs (nuqaba) appointed by God from among the Children of Israel (referenced in Quran 5:12). In Shia tradition, this hadith is understood as a foundational proof for the doctrine of the Twelve Imams from the Prophet's household (Ahl al-Bayt), beginning with Imam Ali and ending with Imam al-Mahdi.
